title: Button combinations on white surfaces: six official examples
scope: Official public design systems and product or marketing pages. These examples illustrate different approaches; they are not a universal palette prescription.
main_white_surface_lesson: Design a combination of surface, text, border, action hierarchy and interaction states. Recognizable brands use black, purple, green and blue primary actions. Brand color need not equal primary-action color, and distinctiveness also comes from typography, shape, spacing and surrounding content.

cases.surface: Polaris App Home web-component examples on white
cases.observation: The current official preview shows a near-black filled primary button with white text, a white secondary button with dark text and a thin border, and an unfilled tertiary button. The green Shopify logo does not determine this button palette.
cases.official_rule: Primary is high emphasis and should be used sparingly; secondary is medium emphasis; tertiary is low emphasis. Critical tone is reserved for destructive actions.
cases.white_surface_lesson: A neutral action family can have clear hierarchy without a saturated brand-colored primary button.
cases.date_and_version_limit: Checked 2026-10-04. The URL tracks latest web components, not a pinned release. Older Polaris React documentation redirects to the new references. This is an App Home example, not every Shopify surface.

cases.surface: Current Korean marketing homepage on white
cases.observation: The primary Get started action uses purple #730394 with white text. Find your plan uses white fill with purple #730394 text and border. Both observed buttons have 4px corner radius. Large black typography and white space form the surrounding context.
cases.official_rule: No global Slack button rule is inferred from this marketing page. These are observed rendered styles, not a published permanent token specification.
cases.white_surface_lesson: One accent can form a family of filled and outlined actions while the rest of the page remains largely neutral.
cases.date_and_version_limit: Observed 2026-10-04. Marketing campaigns, locale and product interfaces may differ. No numbered version is published for this page.

cases.surface: Primer Product UI, current light theme
cases.observation: Published light-theme tokens specify primary green #1F883D with white text, hover #1C8139 and active #197935. Default buttons use #F6F8FA, text #25292E and border #D1D9E0; their hover fill is #EFF2F5 and active fill is #E6EAEF.
cases.official_rule: Success roles include primary buttons and positive states; accent roles include links, selection and focus; danger roles include destructive actions and errors. Use the highest-priority button sparingly, with no more than one in a button group.
cases.white_surface_lesson: Primary green, neutral supporting actions and blue interaction cues can coexist because they have different roles.
cases.date_and_version_limit: Checked 2026-10-04. These documentation values are the active light theme; other themes differ. The page is current documentation rather than a pinned package version.

cases.observation: Published tokens specify primary #0F62FE with white text, hover #0050E6 and active #002D9C. Secondary is charcoal #393939 with white text and hover #474747. Tertiary uses blue text and border with transparent fill.
cases.official_rule: Button variants and their hover, active, focus and disabled appearances use role-specific tokens. Focus combines #0F62FE with an inset white contrast border; disabled button fill is #C6C6C6. Typography, dimensions and spacing are also specified.
cases.white_surface_lesson: Even a familiar blue action becomes a deliberate system when paired with charcoal, outlines and distinct interaction states.
cases.date_and_version_limit: Checked 2026-10-04. The button specification states Last updated Sep 30, 2026. These values apply to the White theme and should not be copied indiscriminately into other themes.

cases.surface: Current button example and functional colors on white
cases.observation: The current Save and continue example has green #0F7A52 fill, white text and square corners. Functional colors include white body background, #0B0C0C body text, #484949 secondary text, #CECECE border and #1A65A6 links.
cases.official_rule: Use functional color tokens for their intended purposes. Yellow #FFDD00 is for focus indication, paired with dark focus text; it is not a general decorative accent. Avoid multiple main calls to action because this weakens their impact and makes the next step less clear.
cases.white_surface_lesson: Green actions, blue links and yellow keyboard focus can be separated by function, supported by strong text and geometry.
cases.date_and_version_limit: Checked 2026-10-04. Button colors were refreshed in GOV.UK Frontend v6.0.0 in Feb 2026; the page also records v6.4.0 changes in Jul 2026. Older green #00703C is not the observed current default.

cases.surface: Current signup screen; historical official design rationale
cases.observation: The current signup screen uses a bright green pill-shaped Next action with black text on a dark page. Social signup actions use white text, dark fill and gray outlines. This is a dark-surface contrast case, not a white-surface template.
cases.official_rule: Spotify Design's 2021 article explains the choice of black foreground on Spotify green to improve contrast while retaining brand character. It also describes sentence-case labels and reduced padding. This historical explanation is not a specification for every current Spotify button.
cases.white_surface_lesson: A bright fill does not automatically call for white text. Consider foreground contrast, shape and label treatment together, and adapt the combination to its actual surface.
cases.date_and_version_limit: Signup screen observed 2026-10-04. Locale and live interface may differ. The official design rationale was published 2021-06-01 and is explicitly historical.

our_proposals.status: Design proposals for comparison, not official brand rules or an approved palette
families: Document/productivity: graphite primary, white outlined secondary, neutral hover surfaces
Collaboration/digital tool: violet primary, violet outline secondary, pale violet supporting hover surfaces
Calm professional tool: deep teal primary, teal outline secondary, pale mint supporting hover surfaces
our_proposals.comparison_guardrail: Keep corresponding actions in both specimens identical in color, shape, label and interaction treatment. Use primary versus secondary styling only for genuine action hierarchy within each specimen.
our_proposals.state_guardrail: Compare default, hover, pressed, focus-visible, loading, disabled and semantic feedback as a complete set. Validate contrast for the actual text, boundaries and focus indicators; saturation alone does not establish quality.
